metadata.title: Why the CLARITY Act is so important for stablecoin customers & issuers

content.text:
Scott Melker speaks with RobinHood (HOOD) SVP of crypto Johann Kerbrat about the importance of the CLARITY Act and stablecoin legislation in the US.
"The Daily Wolf with Scott Melker" airs every day at 12:00 p.m. Tune in for your daily dose of all things crypto.
Make sure to also check out Yahoo Finance's new crypto hub to find the latest crypto-related news.
How much does the Clarity Act mat- matter for you?
I think it does. You know, it's really important for us to have a level playing field in the US. Right now, we have features that are available in some states, some in some are not available in some other states. And I think it's frustrating for our customer. Like they they just want to be able to access the features that they they care about. Um, so I think this clarity act is very important. I think it's a bit, um, ridiculous, you know, that we are blocking it on this idea that stable coins should not uh, generate yield for customers. Uh, you know, if we think about it, a lot of customers, they want the FDIC insurance. They want to be able to think that their money is safe. So they they're already using their banking accounts. They're not trying to to get the the highest yield possible, otherwise they will use feature like like the one we launched. Um so I think at the end of the day, we are we're penalizing people that want to utilize crypto and blockchain technology, uh because for stable coin, it's a lot easier to send, it's a lot easier to transfer 24/7, all of this. So it's not really fair that we are penalizing those customers.
I think they'd be psyched if they got one and a half or 2%.
Right.
Not everybody's looking for seven, they're just looking to not get nothing.
Exactly. Right now, it's a it's the reality, right? It's like you can get nothing or you can get something with cash. So what people are doing is as soon as they get stable, they sell it to get cash and to get a yield. And so it doesn't make sense. It's not it's not optimized for the stable coin issuer, it's not optimized for the customers. Um, and so I think we need to we need to fix this.
I had the misfortune of having to walk into a bank last week to deposit a check and they tried to pitch me on they're like, we can 4X this by opening a savings account, you're yielding. It was, then I looked, it was like 0.1 to 0.4. It's really, hard times, you got to get it where you can, but yeah, it's absurd.
And and that's where, you know, I think tokenization, blockchain technology will will change this traditional finance system. Uh, we're already seeing it. We're already seeing that with blockchain and crypto, a lot of the legacy player are starting to think about it. You saw NYSE, Nasdaq starting to think about what is their crypto strategy. You saw DTC as well. So, I think it's very important that we keep pushing as a company like Robinhood, uh to bring more customers and more retail into this world because that will also bring the institution on the other end and we'll stop this discussion on what if or what is the stable coin strategy and we'll just think about how do we take advantage of this situation.
